chunks: 'Abdullah al-Daysani asked Hisham ibn al-Hakam, saying to him, "Do you have a Lord?" He said, "Yes." He said, "Is He Powerful?" He said, "Yes, Powerful, Compelling." He said, "Is He able to enter the whole world into an egg, without the egg growing larger and without the world becoming smaller?" Hisham said, "Give me respite." So he said to him, "I give you one year's respite." Then he went away from him.

So Hisham rode to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and sought permission to see him, and he granted it. He said to him, 'O son of the Messenger of God! Abdullah al-Daysani came to me with a question for which there is no reliance in answering except upon God and upon you.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'What did he ask you about?' He said, 'He said to me such and such.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'O Hisham! How many are your senses?' He said, 'Five.' He said, 'Which is the smallest of them?' He said, 'The eye (the pupil).' He said, 'And how large is the pupil?' He said, 'Like a lentil seed, or smaller than it.' So he said to him, 'O Hisham, look in front of you and above you, and tell me what you see.' He said, 'I see sky and earth, houses and palaces, open plains and mountains and rivers.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Verily, the One who was able to bring all that you see into a lentil seed or something smaller than it is able to bring the entire world into an egg — without the world becoming smaller and without the egg growing larger.'

So Hisham fell upon him and kissed his hands, his head and his feet, and said, 'This is enough for me, O son of the Messenger of God,' and he departed to his home. The next morning al-Daysani came to him and said, 'O Hisham! I came to you just to greet you, not to demand the answer.' So Hisham said to him, 'If you came to demand it, then here is the answer.'

So al-Daysani went out from him until he came to the door of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), sought permission, and it was granted. When he sat down, he said to him, 'O Ja'far ibn Muhammad! Guide me to my object of worship.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'What is your name?' He then went out and did not tell him his name. His companions said to him, 'Why did you not tell him your name?' He said, 'If I had said to him Abdullah, he would have asked: who is this one whose slave you are?' So they said to him, 'Return to him and say: guide you to your object of worship, but do not ask you about your name.' So he returned to him and said, 'O Ja'far ibn Muhammad! Guide me to my object of worship, and do not ask me my name.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Sit down.' At that moment there was a small servant boy of his with an egg in his palm, playing with it. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Hand me, O boy, the egg.' So he handed it to him.

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) then said to him, 'O Daysani! This is a concealed fortress — it has a thick shell, and beneath the thick shell is a thin membrane, and beneath the thin membrane is flowing gold and dissolved silver. Neither does the flowing gold mix with the dissolved silver, nor does the dissolved silver mix with the flowing gold. So it remains in its state, with no inspector going out from it to report on its soundness, and no corruptor entering it to report on its corruption. It is not known whether it was created for a male or for a female. It will split open revealing the likeness of the colors of peacocks. Do you see any designer for it?'

He (the narrator) said: Then he (al-Daysani) bowed his head down for a long time, then said, 'I bear witness that there is no god except God alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger, and that you are an Imam and a proof from God over His creation, and I am repentant of what I was in.'

key_terms.الدَّيَصَانِيَّ: 'Abdullah al-Daysani - a dualist (Manichaean-influenced) philosopher, contemporary of Imam al-Sadiq; his name is associated with the Daysaniyya sect
key_terms.النَّاظِرُ: The viewer/pupil - the pupil of the eye; used here as the smallest of the senses, yet capable of perceiving the vast universe
key_terms.الْعَدَسَةِ: Lentil seed - the approximate size of the pupil, used by the Imam as a measure for his cosmological argument
key_terms.حُجَّةٌ: Hujja (Proof) - in Shia theology, a title for the Imam as the authoritative proof of God on earth
key_terms.حِصْنٌ مَكْنُونٌ: Concealed fortress - the Imam's description of the egg, highlighting its internal mystery as evidence of divine design
key_terms.مُدَبِّراً: A Designer/Mastermind - the one who plans and governs; the rhetorical question 'Do you see that it has a Designer?' leads al-Daysani to affirm the Creator

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq prove God's existence to the dualist philosopher al-Daysani using an egg?
ai.summary: This narrative recounts two philosophical encounters: first, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) answers a challenge posed to Hisham ibn al-Hakam by the freethinker 'Abdullah al-Daysani about God's omnipotence, using the analogy of the eye perceiving vast things despite its tiny size; second, the Imam directly guides al-Daysani to faith by using an egg as proof of the Creator's existence and design. The hadith was transmitted during the early Abbasid period when theological debates between Muslims and dualist/materialist thinkers like al-Daysani were common. Al-Daysani was a known dualist philosopher who challenged Islamic monotheism, and his conversion at the hands of the Imam represents a victory of Shia kalam (theological argumentation) over heretical philosophy.
